newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales off 0.7 pct in Nov - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales off 0.7 pct in Nov - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales fell 0.7 percent in the four weeks of fiscal November versus October, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales index.

The index rose 5.1 percent compared with the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales rose 6.1 percent in the week ended November 30, compared with the same week a year ago, said the report.
Year-on-year sales growth this week was substantially higher than the level in the past two weeks, said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook Research.
He said most retailers reported heightened sales activity, and noted that the well-publicized shortness of the holiday season this year may have been a contributing factor.
In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, Eileberg said sales on the day after Thanksgiving "probably bode well for the rest of the season."
However, Eilenberg said retailers posting big gains now may see decreases in the fourth week of December due to a mismatch in calendar comparisons.
Department stores are at plan or above plan now, but when the fourth week in December comes, they are going to be up against pre-Christmas a year ago, Eilenberg said.
"That's when the business was great, so they are going to show some poor comparisons," he said.
Eilenberg noted home furnishings, apparel and accessories made strong gains over the past week.
Regionally, all areas showed about the same gains. "It was a well balanced week," Eilenberg added.
